messages.content: I'm planning a trip to Munich. Could you fetch me all available connections for sunday?

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
I’m afraid I don’t have direct access to public‑transport timetables or booking systems through my current set of tools—my sole external capability right now is fetching weather information from the Open‑Meteo API. Because of that, I can’t pull “all available connections” for a specific day directly into our chat.

If you’re looking for train, bus, tram, or metro routes operating around Munich on a particular Sunday, here’s what you could do:

| What you need | Where to look |
|---------------|--------------|
| **Regional & long‑distance trains** (e.g., DB InterCity, ICE, regional services) | [Deutsche Bahn Fahrplan](https://www.bahn.de/fahrplan/) – enter your departure station, destination, and choose “Sundays” as the day. |
| **Munich U-Bahn / S-Bahn** | [MVV Fahrplanauskunft](https://www.mvv-muenchen.de/de/service/fahrplaene.html) – select the line and timetable for Sundays. |
| **Trams & buses** | Same MVV site – use the “Verkehrsmittel suchen” feature or download the official route PDFs. |
| **Bike sharing / car rental availability** | Check local providers’ apps/websites (Nextbike, ShareNow, Sixt, etc.). |

Alternatively, many German cities publish their full weekly timetable online in PDF form, so you can just search “[city] Fahrplan Sonntag pdf”. For example, searching *“Munich U-Bahn Fahrplan Sonntag pdf”* will give you the complete Sunday schedule for each line.

---

### Weather check?

Since I can query the Open‑Meteo API, let me know if you’d like a quick snapshot of tomorrow’s weather in Munich instead. Just tell me whether you prefer temperature, precipitation probability, wind speed, or something else—and I’ll fetch it for you!

We cannot provide actual transport connection info because there's no such tool. So we might respond explaining limitation. Possibly ask clarifying question about what kind of connections they're looking for. Also mention we can't access real-time schedules. Provide suggestion how to find them manually via websites like Deutsche Bahn etc. And also offer weather forecast if needed.

Thus answer: explain inability to fetch transportation schedule due to lack of appropriate tool. Offer alternative resources. Ask clarification.
